Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

positive adjective

hopeful, confident that things will go well

also optimistic, be positive, think positive, a positive attitude, look on the bright side

classical

Cic. Att. 5.18.3: quā rē bonō animō es
Ter. Ad. 696: Bonō animō es

bonō animō esse

phrase: bonō animō es! be positive, cheer up

to be of good heart, to be positive

Also bonum animum habēre (Plaut. Capt. 152), and in a letter, just bonum animum (Cic. Att. 16.12.1). To someone downcast, Bonō animō es! (see cheer up).

Other words

  • bene spērāre — to be hopeful, to expect the best

    phrase (spērō, spērāre) · classical · Cic. Att. 5.14.2: sed bene spērāmus; Nep. Milt. 1.1: dē eō bene spērāre (Lewis & Short)

  • positīvus, positīva, positīvum — positive (in grammar); laid down by convention

    adjective, declension · avoid · post-classical · Gell. 10.4 lemma: nōmina nōn positīva esse sed nātūrālia (Lewis & Short); Traupman 232, 246, 248: gradus positīvus, the positive degree; M-O s.v. positive (math.)

    A term of grammar, the positive degree (gradus positīvus), or of words fixed by convention rather than by nature (Gellius); in Gauss, a positive number (Morgan–Owens). Never “hopeful”.

Examples

  • tamen magnō timōre sum sed bene spērāmus

    all the same, I am very anxious; but we are hopefulCic. Att. 5.14.2

  • sed quid tibi dīcam? bonum animum.

    but what am I to say to you? Keep your spirits up.Cic. Att. 16.12.1

  • Bonō animō es: dūcēs uxōrem hanc. — Hem. — Bonō animō es, inquam.

    Cheer up: you’ll marry her. — What? — Cheer up, I tell you.Ter. Ad. 696

See also cheer up!, hope, cheerful, positive.

SourcesLewis & Short: animus · Lewis & Short: spero · Lewis & Short: positivus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. positive (math.).
